documents.unit: Office of the Provost (Provost-appointed AI Working Group)
documents.title: A Report on AI and the UAB Community
documents.date_or_term: undated in fetch; current as linked (accessed 2026-10-25)
documents.summary: A 2023 provost working-group report that sets no university-wide AI rule. It leaves require-or-prohibit decisions to instructors, asks that choices be stated in the syllabus, sets integrity and attestation rules, and offers sample syllabus statements at prohibit, allow-with-attribution and encourage levels. It also gives recommendations on research, tool vetting, legal issues and training.
documents.stance_why: The report says 'UAB does not dictate that teachers shall require or prohibit the use of generative AI' and hands course decisions to teachers, offering sample prohibit, attribution and encourage statements, so the stance is delegates with tiers.

units.why: The report says UAB leaves the require-or-prohibit choice to teachers: 'UAB does not dictate that teachers shall require or prohibit'. This is a delegation to instructors (P04), a statement of position rather than a command, so modality is informs.
units.anchor: UAB does not dictate that teachers shall require or prohibit the use of generative AI

units.why: Grounds the delegation in academic freedom ('teachers have substantial latitude'). It is the rationale for instructor discretion, so it is coded P04 with informs, not a separate stance type.
units.anchor: teachers have “substantial latitude” in how to teach their courses

units.why: Limits academic freedom: 'All course requirements must adhere to UAB policies as well as the UAB Academic Integrity Code.' Binds every course, and is a compliance-with-existing-rules rule (P77).
units.anchor: All course requirements must adhere to UAB policies as well as the UAB Academic Integrity

units.why: Encourages teachers to make course-level decisions 'appropriate for their specific content and student learning objectives', which ties AI decisions to learning objectives (P83); it also names the consultative route with departments. Chosen over P04 because the focus is alignment with objectives.
units.anchor: make course-level decisions that are appropriate for their specific content and student learning objectives

units.why: Says AI decisions 'should be clearly outlined in the course syllabus and communicated to students', a syllabus-statement expectation for instructors (P09).
units.anchor: should be clearly outlined in the course syllabus and communicated to students

units.why: Empowers teachers to 'Ensure AI cannot be used as a proxy to pass a university course'. It is a teacher power aimed at preventing AI-produced work from earning credit, closest to P19; the type does not capture that this is framed as teacher empowerment.
units.anchor: Ensure AI cannot be used as a proxy to pass a university course.
units.fit_note: Framed as a power teachers hold, not a rule on students; concerns AI standing in for the student's own passing work.

units.why: Teachers are empowered to 'Insist on academic integrity', a general value statement; closest type is P95 (fairness and honesty) although it is phrased as teacher authority.
units.anchor: Insist on academic integrity.
units.fit_note: Phrased as an empowerment of teachers, not as a reason given for a specific AI rule.

units.why: Teachers are empowered to 'Learn and teach how to use AI as part of students' academic and professional development', i.e. teach AI use as a professional skill (P44).
units.anchor: Learn and teach how to use AI as part of students’ academic and professional development.

units.why: Encourages 'openness and sharing of experiences with emerging technologies' among teachers; this resembles faculty communities of learning (P63) but is a general encouragement.
units.anchor: Encourage openness and sharing of experiences with emerging technologies.
units.fit_note: Encourages teachers to share experiences with students and peers; no workshop or community is named.

units.why: Teachers may 'Require complete and accurate documentation of how AI is employed to complete assignments'. This lets instructors demand disclosure of AI use with submissions (P24).
units.anchor: Require complete and accurate documentation of how AI is employed to complete assignments.

units.why: 'Students are encouraged to learn to use AI tools in ways that support their success' welcomes AI use within university guidelines; coded P44 (learn AI as a skill) rather than P02 because it is about learning to use AI, and it is conditional on integrity principles.
units.anchor: Students are encouraged to learn to use AI tools in ways that support their success

units.why: 'They are responsible to know, understand, and comply with AI guidelines established for their courses and presented in the course syllabus' places the duty of learning each course's rules on students (P78).
units.anchor: responsible to know, understand, and comply with AI guidelines established for their courses

units.why: Students are empowered to 'Learn how to use AI as part of their academic and professional development' - the student-side counterpart of teaching AI as a professional skill (P44).
units.anchor: Learn how to use AI as part of their academic and professional development.

units.why: Students may use AI 'at their teachers' direction' to encourage critical thinking, enrich learning and boost creativity. Permission is contingent on the teacher, so the instructor-sets-the-rule type (P04) fits better than P02.
units.anchor: Use AI tools, at their teachers’ direction, to encourage critical thinking, enrich learning, and boost

units.why: Students may 'Document the use of AI as directed by their teachers when completing assignments' - disclosure of AI use, set by the teacher (P24).
units.anchor: Document the use of AI as directed by their teachers when completing assignments.

units.why: Students are empowered to 'Share their own experiences and skills with emerging technologies with teachers and peers' - a general encouragement that no listed type captures.
units.anchor: Share their own experiences and skills with emerging technologies with teachers and peers
units.uncovered_note: Students are encouraged to share their AI experiences and skills with teachers and peers.

units.why: Authors 'must follow guidelines on the use of AI established by the meeting organizer, publisher, sponsor, or oversight agency', deferring to venue and funder rules for scholarship (P62).
units.anchor: must follow guidelines on the use of AI established by the meeting organizer, publisher, sponsor,

units.why: 'Absent specific guidelines, UAB authors should use guidance established by the Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE)' gives a fallback source for research AI rules (P62).
units.anchor: Absent specific guidelines, UAB authors should use guidance established by the Committee on Publication Ethics

units.why: States that misconduct 'is present in an academic work wherever AI assistance has not been disclosed as required', so failure to disclose is itself the violation (P28).
units.anchor: Academic misconduct is present in an academic work wherever AI assistance has not been disclosed

units.why: Says teachers, publishers and the university 'may establish explicit requirements about the use or non-use of AI-generated material', so requirements come from several authorities and instructors can set use or non-use (P04).
units.anchor: may establish explicit requirements about the use or non-use of AI-generated material

units.why: 'By submitting any academic work, students... attest that they have adhered to all established requirements' makes submission an attestation of compliance. P29 (own what you submit) is the nearest type.
units.anchor: By submitting any academic work, students, and all members of the UAB community attest
units.fit_note: An attestation of compliance with all AI requirements, not only ownership of the work.

units.why: Where AI-generated material is allowed, members attest 'that all sources used in preparation, that go beyond common knowledge, are attributed', i.e. attribution of AI-assisted work (P24).
units.anchor: all sources used in preparation, that go beyond common knowledge, are attributed
units.fit_note: Written as an attestation about attributing all sources, of which AI is one.

units.why: Attestation 'That generated material accurately reflects the facts' requires users to verify AI output (P31).
units.anchor: That generated material accurately reflects the facts.

units.why: Untrue attestations, 'whether by intent or negligence', are called deceit and academic misconduct 'subject to review according to UAB's Academic Integrity Code' - misuse is handled as misconduct (P36).
units.anchor: Such behavior constitutes academic misconduct and is subject to review according to UAB’s Academic Integrity

units.why: 'AI systems should be approved for use by a UAB vetting counsel' with legal, compliance, finance, IT and faculty/staff representatives is institutional review of AI tools (P65).
units.anchor: AI systems should be approved for use by a UAB vetting counsel

units.why: The working group 'recommends that the UAB legal office develop policies' on listed AI issues, which names who owns the follow-on policy work (P80).
units.anchor: recommends that the UAB legal office develop policies related to the following issues

units.why: 'Ensure data privacy, security, and compliance with regulations like the GDPR' is a data-protection duty for the institution (P50).
units.anchor: Ensure data privacy, security, and compliance with regulations like the GDPR.

units.why: Notes personal data processed by ChatGPT 'becomes part of the product' and that 'adequate safeguards should be considered' - a privacy warning about AI tools storing prompts (P50).
units.anchor: personal data collected or processed by ChatGPT or similar products becomes part of the product

units.why: Calls for 'Assessing liability and accountability for inaccurate or misleading information generated by ChatGPT' and for disclaimers; no listed type covers institutional liability for AI output.
units.anchor: Clear guidelines and disclaimers should be established to inform users and allocate responsibility.
units.uncovered_note: The university should assess liability for inaccurate AI output and set disclaimers that allocate responsibility.

units.why: 'ChatGPT interfaces should comply with accessibility standards and guidelines such as WCAG 2.1 or 2.2' concerns accessibility of AI tools (P97).
units.anchor: ChatGPT interfaces should comply with accessibility standards and guidelines such as WCAG 2.1 or 2.2.

units.why: Recommends the report be 'disseminated to the UAB community in a timely manner through established communication channels' - spreading the guidance. No listed type covers dissemination.
units.anchor: information from this report be disseminated to the UAB community in a timely manner
units.uncovered_note: Guidance from the report should be disseminated to the UAB community through established channels.

units.why: 'it should be clear that this is a developing situation and that guidance may change and evolve over time' is the provisional-policy statement (P54).
units.anchor: guidance may change and evolve over time

units.why: 'an unprecedented amount of training will be needed at all levels' and everyone 'will need to be trained' states that the institution should provide AI training to teachers, students and staff (P70).
units.anchor: Teachers, researchers, scholars, clinicians, students, administrators, and staff will need to be trained

units.why: Names campus bodies (UAB IT, CTL, eLearning, Libraries, Counsel) that 'will need to be involved in developing and providing this training', and says it should be ongoing and multi-modal (P70).
units.anchor: training be accessible and delivered in multiple modalities and be ongoing

units.why: Sample statement text for all teachers: 'Academic misconduct is present... wherever AI assistance has been used when unauthorized, or when authorized, has not been disclosed' - misuse and nondisclosure are the violations (P28).
units.anchor: has been used when unauthorized, or when authorized, has not been disclosed as required
units.fit_note: Covers both unauthorized use and undisclosed authorized use as misconduct.

units.why: The same sample statement calls such behavior 'deceit' that 'constitutes academic misconduct and is subject to review according to UAB's Academic Integrity Code' (P36).
units.anchor: Deceit constitutes academic misconduct and is subject to review according to UAB’s Academic Integrity Code.

units.why: Sample 'Expect changes' text: rules 'may need to change on short notice' and may affect assignments and evaluation. A provisional-policy notice to students (P54).
units.anchor: the rules that are expressed in this syllabus may need to change on short notice

units.why: Sample prohibition statement: 'The use of generative AI is strictly prohibited in this course.' A blanket default ban (P01).
units.anchor: The use of generative AI is strictly prohibited in this course.

units.why: Sample closed-book statement 'The use of AI tools is not permitted' applies to exams and quizzes (P22).
units.anchor: The use of AI tools is not permitted.

units.why: Sample writing statement: AI tools 'not permitted on writing assignments'. A prose-specific rule separate from code (P18).
units.anchor: The use of generative AI tools is not permitted on writing assignments in this course.

units.why: 'By submitting a writing assignment, you attest that you are the only and original author' - the student attests ownership of submitted work (P29).
units.anchor: you attest that you are the only and original author

units.why: Sample code statement: using AI 'to develop code is strictly prohibited'. Students may not have AI generate code they submit (P19).
units.anchor: The use of generative AI tools to develop code is strictly prohibited in this course.

units.why: 'you attest that you are the only and original author of the code submitted' is an authorship attestation for code (P29).
units.anchor: you attest that you are the only and original author of the code submitted.

units.why: Sample writing statement 'you may submit material that contains AI-generated content... if this use is properly documented' permits AI in prose with documentation. P18 (prose rules) chosen over P24 because it names permitted prose uses (outlines, sections, references).
units.anchor: you may submit material that contains AI-generated content, or is based on or derived from

units.why: Lists allowed uses: 'drafting an outline, preparing individual sections, combining elements, removing redundant parts, and compiling and annotating references' - writing support (P91).
units.anchor: drafting an outline, preparing individual sections, combining elements, removing redundant parts

units.why: 'Your documentation must make the process transparent' requires students to disclose how AI was used (P24).
units.anchor: Your documentation must make the process transparent

units.why: Sample open-book statement permits AI tools on exams or quizzes 'provided you follow our standards for attribution, validation, and transparency'. It is the permissive counterpart of P22; P02 fits, with a fit note.
units.anchor: The use of AI tools is permitted, provided you follow our standards for attribution, validation,
units.fit_note: Permission applies to open-book exams and quizzes and is conditional on attribution, validation and transparency.

units.why: Sample code statement permits AI-generated code 'if this use is properly documented in the comments' - AI code allowed under stated conditions (P16).
units.anchor: you may submit AI-generated code, or code that is based on or derived from AI-generated

units.why: Requires that 'you need to include the prompt and the significant parts of the response' in the code comments - marks AI-derived code in place (P27), and specifies prompt and output (fit_note for P25).
units.anchor: you need to include the prompt and the significant parts of the response
units.fit_note: Also requires the prompt and significant parts of the response (P25 content), not only marking the location.

units.why: 'there is no guarantee that the generated code is correct. It is your responsibility to identify errors in program logic through comprehensive, documented testing' - verify AI output (P31).
units.anchor: It is your responsibility to identify errors in program logic through comprehensive, documented testing.

units.why: Says generated code 'may have significant scope for improvement, regarding separation of concerns and avoiding repetitions' and that the submission must meet standards - a caution about AI code quality, nearest P31.
units.anchor: generated code, even if syntactically correct, may have significant scope for improvement
units.fit_note: Quality concern (design, repetition), not only factual correctness.

units.why: 'We encourage the use of such AI resources to inform yourself about the field... and to help your learning' welcomes AI use for learning, a permit-or-encourage default (P02).
units.anchor: We encourage the use of such AI resources to inform yourself about the field

units.why: Principle 1: 'AI generated submissions cannot achieve a passing grade'. Students may not rely on AI-produced submissions; nearest type P19 with a fit note, since the rule is expressed as a grade consequence.
units.anchor: AI generated submissions cannot achieve a passing grade.
units.fit_note: Stated as a grading consequence (a failing grade), not an outright ban on using AI.

units.why: Gives the reason: students must be 'competent to surpass generative AI in the future - whether in academia, research, the workplace'. A career-based reason for requiring human competence (P94).
units.anchor: whether in academia, research, the workplace, or other domains of society.

units.why: 'we will produce, analyze, and provide AI-generated sample solutions. Your task will be to surpass them' sets an AI-derived baseline for grading, a redesign of assessment around AI (P35).
units.anchor: we will produce, analyze, and provide AI-generated sample solutions. Your task will be to surpass

units.why: Principle 2: 'You are taking full responsibility for AI-generated materials as if you had produced them yourself' - students own what they submit (P29).
units.anchor: You are taking full responsibility for AI-generated materials as if you had produced them yourself

units.why: 'ideas must be attributed, and facts must be true' requires attribution and fact-checking of AI contributions; P24 chosen, fit note for the truth requirement.
units.anchor: ideas must be attributed, and facts must be true
units.fit_note: Also requires that facts in AI-generated material be true (verification).

units.why: 'A portion of your term grade will evaluate your documentation of AI use throughout the course' makes documentation of AI use part of the grade (P35, grading around AI process).
units.anchor: A portion of your term grade will evaluate your documentation of AI use throughout the

units.why: 'By keeping track of your AI use and sharing your experiences' asks students to keep a record of their AI use over the course (P26).
units.anchor: By keeping track of your AI use and sharing your experiences

units.why: Report's introduction says AI 'offers exciting opportunities for personalized learning, efficient assessment, enhanced accessibility, intelligent tutoring' - stated benefits (P87).
units.anchor: offers exciting opportunities for personalized learning, efficient assessment, enhanced accessibility, intelligent tutoring

units.why: Names 'data privacy, authorship attribution, potential machine-induced biases, and job displacement' as concerns - ethical and bias concerns (P53).
units.anchor: Ethical and legal concerns arise regarding data privacy, authorship attribution, potential machine-induced biases

units.why: 'It is incumbent upon UAB to develop policies and procedures' and AI must be 'ethically deployed' and used 'to enhance rather than replace the essential roles of humans' - a framework preamble (P56).
units.anchor: used as a tool to enhance rather than replace the essential roles of humans

units.why: 'it is essential that students, educators, researchers, scholars, and clinicians are trained to maximize the benefits and minimize the harms' - the training rationale (P70).
units.anchor: it is essential that students, educators, researchers, scholars, and clinicians are trained

units.why: The attestation says the authors 'consulted with additional members of the UAB community' and 'employed AI technology as a resource in its development' - how the report was made, including AI use (P84).
units.anchor: employed AI technology as a resource in its development

units.why: Reports that the group 'reviewed the AI responses of other universities' - benchmarking against peers (P88).
units.anchor: reviewed the AI responses of other universities

units.why: LLMs 'have demonstrated a propensity to hallucinate and create output text that seems to be true or accurate but is actually false' - output can be wrong (P31).
units.anchor: propensity to ‘hallucinate’ and create output text that seems to be true or accurate but

units.why: 'LLMs can also create output that many would find offensive and biased due to inherent bias in the training' - bias concern (P53).
units.anchor: output that many would find offensive and biased due to inherent bias in the training

units.why: 'Cheating: AI can be used to generate answers to test questions, allowing students to cheat' lists cheating as an integrity risk; it is a description of risk with no matching type.
units.anchor: AI can be used to generate answers to test questions, allowing students to cheat on
units.uncovered_note: Names AI-enabled cheating on exams and homework as a threat to academic integrity.

units.why: 'Plagiarism: AI can generate research papers and essays, making it easier for students to engage in plagiarism' - another integrity risk statement without a matching type.
units.anchor: AI can generate research papers and essays, making it easier for students to engage in
units.uncovered_note: Names AI-enabled plagiarism of essays and papers as a threat to academic integrity.

units.why: 'AI can reduce the incentive for students to think critically and creatively' - AI shortcuts the thinking that builds skill (P41).
units.anchor: AI can reduce the incentive for students to think critically and creatively

units.why: 'Overreliance on AI technologies may diminish critical thinking and problem-solving skills among students' - outsourcing practice harms learning (P41).
units.anchor: Overreliance on AI technologies may diminish critical thinking and problem-solving skills among students

units.why: Concern that 'Automation of Grading... lack of human interaction may limit educators' ability to provide meaningful feedback'. Related to humans grading (P46) but only a concern, not a rule, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: the lack of human interaction may limit educators' ability to provide meaningful feedback and assessment
units.uncovered_note: Warns that AI-automated grading may lose human feedback and nuance.

units.why: 'AI can potentially aid teachers in grading assignments and delivering feedback' - possible instructor use of AI for teaching work (P59).
units.anchor: AI can potentially aid teachers in grading assignments and delivering feedback

units.why: Equity impact: 'Not all students, staff, or institutions have equal access to the necessary hardware, software, or high-speed internet' - access gap (P51).
units.anchor: Not all students, staff, or institutions have equal access to the necessary hardware, software, or

units.why: 'Many AI technologies are developed and optimized for English language users, which can marginalize non-English speakers' - bias and harm concern (P53).
units.anchor: developed and optimized for English language users, which can marginalize non-English speakers

units.why: 'At present, the person entering the prompts and text materials retains the copyright' - a fact about ownership of AI inputs and outputs (P52).
units.anchor: the person entering the prompts and text materials retains the copyright

units.why: 'The use of patented or copyrighted material as a prompt for the AI may compromise claim or security of those materials' - IP risk of prompting (P52).
units.anchor: may compromise claim or security of those materials

units.why: 'how the use of AI impacts the domains of patent applications, copyright licensing, and trademarks is unclear' - open IP questions (P52).
units.anchor: how the use of AI impacts the domains of patent applications, copyright licensing, and trademarks

units.why: AI 'can improve accessibility for students with disabilities by providing alternative formats, closed captioning, and text-to-speech' - AI as an accessibility aid (P97).
units.anchor: AI technologies can improve accessibility for students with disabilities

units.why: 'Overreliance on AI in teaching may reduce the opportunities for face-to-face interaction and personalized support from instructors' - a human-contact concern with no matching type.
units.anchor: Overreliance on AI in teaching may reduce the opportunities for face-to-face interaction
units.uncovered_note: Warns that overreliance on AI in teaching may reduce human interaction and personalized instructor support.

units.why: 'Integrating AI in teaching may raise concerns about job displacement among educators' - labor concern (P53).
units.anchor: Integrating AI in teaching may raise concerns about job displacement among educators

units.why: 'AI systems can autonomously generate content, making it challenging to discern the contributions of human researchers' - authorship attribution in scholarship (P62).
units.anchor: making it challenging to discern the contributions of human researchers
units.fit_note: Concerns credit and attribution of authorship, not a rule for a venue.

units.why: 'Lack of literacy about how AI models are trained may lead to less robust scholarly and scientific output if users do not develop appropriate methods for verifying results' - verification in research (P31).
units.anchor: if users do not develop appropriate methods for verifying results of AI-enabled tools

documents.title: AI Resources (Syllabus Guidance and sample statements)
documents.summary: The teaching center's AI resources page gives instructors sample syllabus statements: statements for all teachers, an allow-with-attribution set, an encourage set with three principles, and a prohibit set. It sets no rule of its own and points to the Provost working-group report and to workshops.

notes: The UAB Generative AI and UAB Policy page was inaccessible (404), so it is not coded. The provost report's clinical and medical sections (FDA clearance, radiology, EHR) were skipped as not about teaching or learning. CTL sample statements repeat the report's; both documents were coded on their own. The computer-code allow-with-attribution sample text appears only in the report; the CTL page omits it.
